author: Karl Rock
description:
One of the most touching details at the Chaukhandi Tombs is that many families were buried side by side.

As generations passed, new tombs were built next to older ones, creating family burial plots that have survived for centuries. Walking among them gives you a glimpse into the lives, traditions, and legacies of the communities that once lived here.

The Chaukhandi Tombs, near Karachi in Sindh, date from the 15th to 18th centuries and are famous for their beautifully carved sandstone monuments.
title: Families Buried Together in Pakistan

author: Karl Rock
description:
How do you build a stone tomb that can survive for more than 500 years?

At the Chaukhandi Tombs in Sindh, Pakistan, the answer is surprisingly simple. Instead of carving each monument from a single block, the tombs were carefully built by stacking layers of sandstone, creating strong, beautifully detailed structures that have stood the test of time.

It's an impressive example of the craftsmanship and engineering of the artisans who built one of Pakistan's most remarkable historical sites.
title: 500-Year-Old Engineering in Pakistan!
